final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral USMCA package: 75% RVC effective January 1, 2020 with audits/penalties starting April 1; tri-national commission with direct worker complaints and proactive audits; Canada's dairy concessions (15-20% cheese/butter cuts) locked in text; Chapter 19 preserved; 6-year sunset replaced by review mechanism. Canada signed under pressure after securing dairy floor numbers and April 1 grace period.
minority_objections: Canada initially demanded RVC phase-in (70-73-75%) but was overruled by USTR's day-one 75% ultimatum
Dairy_ag pushed for deeper tariff cuts (25% cheese/butter) but settled for 15-20% to close the deal
Supply_chain_mfr warned that linking labor enforcement to trade remedies would freeze capex
key_conflicts: Canada's demand for RVC phase-in vs. USTR's insistence on day-one 75% (resolved via April 1 audit delay)
Congress/labor_union demand for independent enforcement vs. Mexico's resistance to U.S. inspectors (resolved via tri-national commission)
Dairy_ag's market-access demands vs. Canada's supply-management red line (resolved at 15-20% cuts)
Auto_industry's compliance-cost concerns vs. enforcement credibility (resolved via 90-day grace + unannounced audits)
key_concessions: Canada accepted 75% RVC day-one in exchange for April 1 audit start and dairy floor in agreement text
Mexico accepted tri-national commission with direct worker complaints (no labor ministry filter)
USTR replaced hard sunset with 6-year review mechanism to address business uncertainty
Canada opened dairy market (15-20% cheese/butter cuts, 3.6% fluid milk) while preserving supply management core
Auto_industry accepted unannounced audits in exchange for 72-hour documentation window
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain unchanged (preserved)
Congress/labor_union: no Mexico labor ministry gatekeeping on enforcement (achieved via tri-national commission)
Supply_chain_mfr: labor enforcement cannot become tariff weapon against Canada (locked as separate domains)
USTR: 75% RVC floor non-negotiable, no phase-in of the percentage itself (enforced)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Continuous-readiness compliance infrastructure costs from unannounced audits (auto_industry raised but accepted)
Political backlash in Canada from dairy concessions despite supply-management preservation
Worker retaliation risk in Mexico despite direct complaint mechanism (labor_union noted but commission proactive audits added as mitigation)
Vehicle price increases from $2B+ supply-chain restructuring costs (auto_industry flagged but not addressed in final package)
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification vote outcome depends on perceived enforcement credibility of tri-national commission
Canadian Parliament ratification hinges on dairy sector acceptance of 15-20% cuts
Actual compliance costs and supply-chain disruption from day-one 75% RVC with only 4-month grace period
Effectiveness of tri-national commission in practice (proactive audit frequency, penalty enforcement)
Six-year review outcome and potential for non-renewal creating new sunset uncertainty
uncertainty_notes: Tri-national commission operational details remain unspecified (composition, voting rules, penalty enforcement mechanism). Proactive audit trigger criteria not defined. Mid-term RVC reviews (year 2/4) added but scope/adjustment authority unclear. Actual tariff cut percentages on cheese/butter stated as ranges (15-20%) not precise numbers.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC was the central negotiation point across all rounds; Canada's phase-in demand vs. USTR's day-one ultimatum drove the April 1 audit compromise that closed the deal
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress explicitly stated 'won't ratify' without independent verification; tri-national commission with direct worker complaints and proactive audits was the core enforcement architecture that enabled ratification
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada refused to sign until dairy tariff cuts were 'in writing'; dairy_ag's market-access demands vs. Canada's supply-management created final blocking tension resolved at 15-20% cuts
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'stays off the table entirely' and 'non-negotiable' but it was preserved without negotiation—acknowledged as red line but never contested, so raised not decisive
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: USTR's 6-year review mechanism with 90-day rollover explicitly replaced hard sunset to address business uncertainty; supply_chain_mfr demanded clarity before capex commitment
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress repeatedly stated 'won't ratify' weak enforcement or bilateral workaround; ratification constraints drove tri-national commission design, enforcement sequence, and pressure on Canada to sign
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto_industry and supply_chain_mfr raised $2B+ retooling costs, compliance infrastructure, and capex freeze risks, but these were acknowledged and then absorbed rather than driving concessions—raised but not decisive
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's 'sign today or we finalize bilateral with Mexico' ultimatum and Mexico's 'we're locked in, Canada join or we move' created the leverage that forced Canada's dairy concessions and April 1 acceptance
